sheet-1.description: The map part of sheet 1 is the southern end of Cape May Court House, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The rest of the sheet holds the title cartouche, notes on water and fire facilities, a key map at 800 ft to an inch, a location map of New Jersey, the legend and the street and specials index; none of that is georeferenced. The part runs from Railroad Avenue along the west edge to Main Street and a strip east of Main, and from Carr, an arbitrary and not yet opened street at the north, past Schoolhouse Lane, Atlantic Avenue and Pacific Avenue to vacant ground south of Pacific. 2nd Street runs between Atlantic and Pacific in the middle of the part. The large block north of Schoolhouse Lane holds the Cape May Court House Grammar School, a frame building, and the Cape May Court House High School, a brick building. The other blocks are thinly built with frame dwellings, outbuildings and garages, mostly along Atlantic Avenue, Pacific Avenue, 2nd Street and Main Street; large lots south of Pacific are still open. Street widths are lettered at the edges of the blocks (60 ft for Atlantic and Pacific, 50 ft for Main and 2nd Street). House numbers on this sheet are marked as arbitrary in the index. A heavy line divides the map from the index above it and to its right, and sheet numbers 2 and 5 at the top edge show where those sheets join. The scale bar and copyright note sit inside the bottom of the part.
notes: Railroad Av is today Reading Avenue; Atlantic Av and Pacific Av are West and East Atlantic Avenue and West and East Pacific Avenue; 2nd St is part of South Boyd Street; Main is South Main Street.
Schoolhouse Lane at Main is drawn about 15 m south of today's School House Lane / South Main Street junction; that junction was left out of the fit.
Carr is marked 'arbitrary' and 'not opened'; no modern street matches it.

map. Sheet 1 carries the title cartouche, water and fire notes, an 800 ft key map of the town, a state location map, the legend and the street and specials index (top half, not georeferenced); the bottom-left part is a map at 100 ft to an inch: Schoolhouse Lane, Atlantic Av, Pacific Av between Railroad Av and Main St, with 2nd St, Carr (not opened) and the Grammar and High Schools. One part.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the west side of Main Street in the centre of Cape May Court House, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, from Mechanic Street and its eastern continuation Hereford Avenue at the north to Carr, an arbitrary street not yet opened, at the south, and from Boyd Street at the west to a strip of lots east of Main. Hand Avenue and Stites Avenue cross from Boyd to Main. The commercial centre lies along Mechanic Street: a row of stores and dwellings with the post office, a doctor's office, an old foundry, a painting shop, the Gazette Block on the corner of Main, the Bellevue Hotel with its pool room, a carriage house and stable, a bakery and bake house. Along Main Street are garages with capacities of 20 and 40 cars, dwellings and a private lane; the First Baptist Church stands at Hand Avenue and Main with a smaller church and a wagon shed beside it. The southern half of the sheet, block 29, is mostly open with a few dwellings along Main. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in Mechanic Street and Main Street, with fire hydrants. Main is lettered 92 ft wide at the north and 55 to 60 ft further south. Sheet numbers 3, 5 and 1 at the edges mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Hereford Av is today East Mechanic Street; Hand Av is West Hand Avenue; Boyd is South Boyd Street; Main is South Main Street.
Carr is marked 'arbitrary' and 'not open'.
map, 50 ft. Main St between Mechanic/Hereford Av and Carr (arbitrary, not opened), west to Boyd St: Hand Av, Stites Av, Bellevue Hotel, post office, First Baptist Church, garages. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the county seat's civic centre, drawn at 50 ft to an inch: the blocks between Boyd Street on the west and Main Street, with a strip of lots east of Main, from Mechanic Street and Hereford Avenue at the south to Romney Place, with lots beyond Romney marked 'no exposure' at the north edge. Church Street runs from Boyd to Main between them. The block east of Church and west of Main holds the county buildings: the Court House, the clerk's and surrogate's offices and the jail with the sheriff's dwelling, fireproof construction, and the fire department building, which also serves as the voting place and carries the fire alarm. The M.E. Church and the Methodist Church Hall stand on Church Street. Along Mechanic Street is a row of stores with a wall paper shop, drug store, motion picture house, hardware and furniture, stoves and tin shop, lodge rooms and the First National Bank with the Commercial League above it. Dwellings with sheds and stables line Boyd Street, Romney Place and the east side of Main, where there is a law office and a carpentry and lumber shed. Main Street is lettered 72 ft and, near Mechanic, 107 ft wide. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the streets.
notes: Boyd is today North Boyd Street; Main is North Main Street; Romney Pl east of Main is East Romney Place; Hereford Av is East Mechanic Street.
Court House, county offices and jail, M.E. Church and First National Bank are on this sheet.
map, 50 ft. Boyd St to Main St and east of Main, between Mechanic/Hereford Av and Romney Pl: Church St, court house, county buildings and jail, M.E. Church, First National Bank. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the blocks west of Boyd Street between Mechanic Street at the south and Romney Place, with lots north of Romney at the top edge. Church Street crosses the part from Poplar Street to Boyd. Railroad Avenue, about 115 ft wide here, carries the P. & R. Ry (Atlantic City Division) through the middle of the part, with its freight depot and passenger depot and platform beside the track at Mechanic Street. East of the railroad is the W. J. Tyler coal and lumber yard with lumber sheds, coal bins on a trestle served by a siding, a lime and cement shed and scales. West of the railroad, along Poplar Street, are dwellings, an auto repair shop, an ice house, storage and the Hereford Lodge of the I.O.O.F. Dwellings and stables fill the lots along Boyd Street, Romney Place and Mechanic Street. Two private drives run west of the railroad. A heavy line cuts off the top-left corner of the sheet, which holds an inset of a glass works one mile away (part 2, not placed). Water pipes are drawn in Mechanic Street and Boyd Street.
notes: Railroad Av is today Reading Avenue, which runs about 7 to 15 m east of the former rail line; Boyd is North Boyd Street; Poplar is Poplar Street.
The lodge is lettered 'Hereford Lodge No 108 (I.O.O.F.)'; the sheet 1 index gives No. 128.

map, 50 ft. Part 1: Poplar St to Boyd St between Mechanic St and Romney Pl, Railroad Av with the P.&R. Ry (A.C. Divn) and the W. J. Tyler coal and lumber yard. Part 2: inset at top left, Cape May Glass Co. Factory G (abandoned), 'Located 1 mile S.W. of Court Ho.', with P.&R. tracks and sidings only; no street.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Cape May Glass Co. Factory G (abandoned), located 1 mile S.W. of Court House (no street junction; only P.&R. tracks and sidings, and the location is given only as 1 mile S.W.; needs a modern feature matching the tracks or the plant site (former rail line south-west of town); step 6b).

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the blocks between Railroad Avenue and Boyd Street from Mechanic Street at the north to Carr, an arbitrary street not yet opened, at the south, and a strip west of the railroad between Hand Avenue and Carr. Hand Avenue and Stites Avenue cross the part. The P. & R. Ry (Atlantic City Division) runs down the middle of Railroad Avenue, which is lettered 60 to 70 ft wide. Along Mechanic Street are dwellings, a paint shop, a hardware and stove shop with a tin shop, a feed warehouse and a 2000-gallon water tank on a roof. The Texas Co. gasoline tanks stand on Railroad Avenue at Hand Avenue, and the Standard Oil Co. oil well and gasoline tanks south of Stites Avenue; a railroad section house stands beside the track. The large blocks 17, 25 and 28 are mostly open, with scattered dwellings. West of the railroad a row of dwellings faces Hand Avenue and the blocks to the south are vacant. A heavy line encloses the inset of the Cape May Glass Co. at the top left (part 2).
notes: Railroad Av is today Reading Avenue; Hand Av is West Hand Avenue; Boyd is South Boyd Street.
The P.&R. track is the former Cape May Branch, now disused.

map, 50 ft. Part 1: Railroad Av (P.&R. Ry in the street) to Boyd St between Mechanic St and Carr (arbitrary), Hand Av and Stites Av, Texas Co. and Standard Oil Co. tanks. Part 2: inset at top left, Cape May Glass Co. bottle works on Schoolhouse Lane west of the P.&R. Ry.

sheet-5-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 5 is an inset in the top-left corner of the sheet, enclosed by a heavy line and drawn at 50 ft to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows the works of the Cape May Glass Co., manufacturers of glass bottles, on the south side of Schoolhouse Lane just west of the P. & R. Ry (Atlantic City Division), whose track runs along the right edge of the inset; a siding crosses the works diagonally. The plant comprises a furnace building with lehrs, a packing room, batch rooms, several warehouses, an office, a box shop, a mould room, a pump house and a 7000-gallon tank. A note gives the night watchman, electric lighting, steam power, oil fuel for the glass manufacture, and a steam pump supplied from a 6-inch driven well. Ground on all other sides is marked 'vacant beyond'. The inset has no street junction of its own and is placed from the junction of Schoolhouse Lane with Railroad Avenue as drawn on sheet 1.
notes: Placed from one point carried from sheet 1 (Schoolhouse Lane at the centre of Railroad Avenue) and a derived point at the scale and rotation of sheet 5 part 1; low confidence.
Sheet 4 part 2 shows a second, abandoned Cape May Glass Co. plant (Factory G) one mile south-west of the Court House.

map, 50 ft. Part 1: Railroad Av (P.&R. Ry in the street) to Boyd St between Mechanic St and Carr (arbitrary), Hand Av and Stites Av, Texas Co. and Standard Oil Co. tanks. Part 2: inset at top left, Cape May Glass Co. bottle works on Schoolhouse Lane west of the P.&R. Ry.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the west side of the town between Goshen Road and Railroad Avenue, from Church Street at the north to Hand Avenue at the south. Mechanic Street crosses the sheet; Goshen Road comes in from the north-west and Bayside or Dias Road leaves Mechanic Street towards the south-west, meeting Hand Avenue at the bottom left. Poplar Street runs north from Mechanic to Church. The sheet is residential: frame dwellings with stables, sheds, coops and garages on long narrow lots along Mechanic Street, Goshen Road, Bayside or Dias Road and Hand Avenue, with storage and lumber sheds near Poplar Street. At the Railroad Avenue edge, beside the P. & R. tracks, are the water works of the Cape May Court House Light & Water Co.: two water tanks, one of 20,000 gallons 50 ft above ground, a pump house, and an engine room with engine, dynamo and boiler. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in Mechanic Street, Hand Avenue and Railroad Avenue. Lots north of Church Street are marked 'no exposure'.
notes: Bayside or Dias R'd is today Dias Creek Road; Mechanic west of Goshen is West Mechanic Street; Hand Av is West Hand Avenue; Railroad Av is Reading Avenue.
Church Street / Goshen Road was hand-picked from the drawn edges.
map, 50 ft. Goshen Rd and Bayside or Dias Rd to Railroad Av, between Church St and Hand Av, with Poplar St and Mechanic St; Cape May Court House Light & Water Co. water works. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the western edge of the town along the West Jersey & Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), which runs down the sheet inside Pennsylvania Avenue, lettered 85 ft wide, with a siding and coal bins to the east. Mechanic Street enters from the east and ends near the railroad; Hand Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet; Goshen Road cuts across the top-right corner, and Bayside or Dias Road appears at the bottom-right corner. West of the railroad stands the Reliance Leather Co., makers of Releco Kid (patent leather), marked not in operation: drying ovens, mixing, coating and tacking rooms, storage buildings, a boiler and a stock and finishing building. Beside the track are the railroad's freight and passenger depot with its platform, a shelter and a section house. Dwellings and stables line Mechanic Street and Hand Avenue; the large blocks 2 and 15 are mostly open. Land to the west and north is marked 'no exposure'.
notes: Pennsylvania Av is taken to be today's Haman Avenue at Hand Avenue; the railroad is the razed West Jersey & Seashore main line.
Placed as a helmert from two points along Hand Avenue (one detected, one hand-picked) and a block corner carried from sheet 6; low confidence.

map, 50 ft. Pennsylvania Av and the W.J.&S.S.R.R. (P.R.R.) between the north sheet edge and Hand Av, Mechanic St east to sheet 6, Goshen Rd at top right; Reliance Leather Co. (Releco Kid) works, P.R.R. freight depot. One part.
